title: Patellar Instability

positions.as_written: Take the history: the age at first episode, how many episodes, what position the knee was in, and whether the patella had to be put back.
Ask about family history and about generalised laxity, since both are common in this group.
Assess generalised laxity with the standard joint assessment, because it changes the interpretation of the knee findings.
Assess patellar translation in extension and at thirty degrees, comparing with the other side.
Assess apprehension on lateral translation, which is the finding that distinguishes instability from laxity.
